rejected.title: Editing paragraphs for control
card: Focus
A paragraph should have one clear focus, shown in its topic sentence. Cut or move any sentence that drifts to another idea.
Sentences
Vary the length and the openings of sentences so the writing does not feel flat. Check each one for correct grammar, spelling and punctuation.
Vocabulary
Replace vague words such as good, bad, thing or a lot with precise ones. Example: "a good result" can become "a record-breaking result".
Editing means reading your draft again and fixing these three areas so the paragraph stays in control of its point.
rejected.remember: Edit for one focus, varied and correct sentences, and precise words.

a.q: A paragraph about the benefits of cycling to school includes a sentence about the price of cars. What should the writer do?
opts: Cut it or move it, as it drifts from the paragraph's focus
Keep it, as extra detail always makes a paragraph stronger
Make the sentence longer so it fits in with the others
Swap the vague words in it for more precise ones
a.why: Editing for control keeps one focus, so a sentence on another idea should be cut or moved. Making words more precise is a good edit, but it does not fix a sentence that is off topic.
a.clue: Think about what the paragraph is meant to be about.

b.q: Tom's draft says the clean-up was good and the volunteers did a lot of things. Which edit improves the vocabulary most?
opts: The clean-up was inspiring and volunteers collected rubbish
The clean-up was very good and volunteers did many things
The clean-up was good, and the volunteers did a lot
The clean-up was good and volunteers did lots of stuff
b.why: The edit that says the clean-up was inspiring and volunteers collected rubbish swaps vague words (good, things) for precise ones. The others still use vague words such as good, many things, a lot and stuff, and adding very does not make good any more precise.
b.clue: Which option replaces vague words with exact ones?

flags: Question a, wording: A sentence about the price of cars could be on topic in a paragraph about the benefits of cycling, since saving money compared with buying a car is a common benefit. Make the drifting sentence clearly unrelated, for example one about car colours or engine sizes.
